summary: Los Angeles County lookout on Los Pinetos Peak, a Forest Service and county forestry co-op opened 1934; abandoned by the 1940s over smog; only the slab by 1964.

facts.design: open timber tower about 10 feet high with a glass-enclosed cab (sources disagree on cab size)
facts.status_note: Angeles Adventures lists the lookout as demolished; only the concrete slab remained by 1964
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service with the Los Angeles County Forestry Department (co-operative)

staffing.status: named staff in 1938 and 1958; the same source says it was abandoned by the 1940s (disputed)

visit.trail_note: The Santa Clara Divide Road runs past the peak; Angeles Adventures says it could be driven up to LA County Fire Camp 9 in 2019. Summit access is not described.

events.note: Opened by the U.S. Forest Service; a co-operative effort with the Los Angeles County Forestry Department
Western Air Express Boeing 247D crashed on the north slope of the peak; the victims were carried to the lookout tower
Lee Park named as lookout staff
Source says abandoned 'by the 1940s'; only the decade is given, so the year shown is the start of that decade
Bill Nelson named as lookout staff; conflicts with the 1940s abandonment in the same source
Only the concrete slab that held the lookout remained

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Angeles Adventures gives 1935-1960s in its table but 1934 in its text; the Forest Lookouts page also says 1934. The record uses 1934.
Angeles Adventures' text describes a glass-enclosed cab of twenty square feet, while its table lists a standard 14 by 14 foot cab. The record keeps the design general and flags the disagreement.
Angeles Adventures names a 1958 staffer but also says the lookout was abandoned by the 1940s. Both statements are kept and staffing is marked disputed.

sources.title: Los Pinetos Nike Missile Site (HAER No. CA-56)
sources.publisher: Historic American Engineering Record, National Park Service

notes_for_editor: Nearly all lookout-specific detail rests on one source, Angeles Adventures, whose own dates, cab size and 1958 staffing conflict; all three are kept as disputed. The 1937 crash comes from that source alone. The Nike site is a separate installation about four miles away and appears only for context. Brief status gone matches all sources. The brief's agency line is consistent with the Forest Lookouts header.
